GRFX Replacement Parts

Replacing a sensor or a control box on a GRFX system? This page has the parts.

The water temp sender reads 100-300 degrees F, and the solid-state oil pressure sender reads 0-150 psi. Each comes with a 10 ft wire harness. The small block Chevy oil pressure adaptor is machined in the USA and gives the sensor more room.

You'll also find a replacement GRFX control box, a 16K PPM pulse generator, a Ford and Tremec adaptor, a BIM daisy-chain cable and a 3 ft display harness for the GRFX display and GLC clock. Bushings come in several sizes, including metric thread versions with a crush washer.

130070: Small Block Chevy Oil Pressure Adapter 

It’s no secret that the small block Chevy doesn’t allow much space for an oil pressure sensor. For years, enthusiasts hit the hardware store in search of a few brass fittings to move the sensor up and away from the intake and distributor. This one-piece machined adapter gives you the clearance and flexibility you need in one convenient solution. The 130070 is machined in the USA with a male 1/8” NPT thread to fit your block, plus two female 1/8” NPT threads to accept the sensor of your choice. The female ports are at 45 and 90 degrees, allowing maximum flexibility for a variety of situations. A 1/8” NPT pipe-plug is included to block off the unused port. 

130071: Ford Gen1 and Gen2 Coyote Oil Pressure Adapter

Ford’s Coyote engines are coming in to their own in the hot rod world, but transplanting one into your classic is not without road blocks. One of which is connecting instrumentation; oil pressure data is not available on the CAN/Bus system for the BIM-01-2 interface to read, so the supplied 1/8”NPT sensor must be installed. This brass adapter is machined in the USA and features ¼” NPTF male threads to fit your Gen 1 and Gen 2 Coyote block, along with female threads to accommodate the stock sensor. On the side is a 1/8” NPTF port to accept the Dakota Digital oil pressure sensor. No drilling and tapping required; simply thread in and go!

*A range of 2016 GEN II F-150 engines used a GEN III type of pressure switch (identified with a black connector body), which contained a 12mm male thread.  The 130071 is not compatible with this variation, nor GEN III applications.
